Cc: payments@lumenix.io
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Lumenix payment sent (remittance attached) - July invoices

Hi Diego / Redwood payments team,

We initiated an outbound transfer earlier today covering the July invoices. Attached is our remittance PDF and bank advice. Quick summary:
- Total payment: EUR 48,250.00 (single transfer)
- Invoices referenced: LUM-INV-202605, LUM-INV-202606, LUM-INV-202607

Note: Our ERP shows LUM-INV-202605 at EUR 12,500 and LUM-INV-202606 at EUR 15,750. The remaining balance was applied to LUM-INV-202607 but our team flagged a difference of EUR 250 (our side shows 20,000; your portal shows 19,750). Can you confirm allocation and whether you require an adjusted remittance?

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: Lumenix_Remittance_2026-07-13.pdf (PDF, 84KB)], [Attachment: Lumenix_Bank_Advice_071326.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

Thanks,
Sophie Clark
Head of Revenue Operations
Lumenix Inc.
Sophie.Clark@lumenix.io

>

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@lumenix.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix payment sent (remittance attached) - July invoices

Sophie —

Appreciate the remittance. Quick update from treasury: we see an incoming EUR 48,250 on 2026-07-14 but it arrived with a short reference code (TRACE: 7X9L-LLN). Our cash application queue matched LUM-INV-202605 and LUM-INV-202606 correctly but only applied EUR 19,750 against LUM-INV-202607, leaving EUR 250 unapplied.

Could you check whether the outgoing transfer included a bank fee deduction or a credit memo that would account for the EUR 250? If nothing on your side, we can hold the ledger entry as "pending allocation" while we confirm with our bank.

Next steps (suggested):
- Sophie: confirm if any bank charges/fees or internal credit memos applied on your side (yes/no)
- Vanessa (cc): if possible, grid a brief ledger note so the customer-facing portal reflects a pending hold and not a hard discrepancy
- Laura (cc): can treasury accept the hold for up to 7 business days pending proof? We want to avoid writing off the 250 prematurely.

Attachment: [Attachment: screenshot-cashapply-queue.png (PNG, 28KB)]

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwood.com

Diego,

Checked with our treasury. Bank confirms the outgoing payment was EUR 48,250 gross; our bank debited the account for EUR 48,500 due to a correspondent bank fee of EUR 250 which Lumenix took on (line item: CORRESP_FEE_250). The amount delivered to recipient was therefore EUR 48,250 and the beneficiary bank deposited EUR 48,000 against invoice LUM-INV-202607 in their sweep step —looks like the intermediary fee hit the delivered amount before our beneficiary string mapped across all three invoices.

We are attaching a signed bank advice PDF showing the CORRESP_FEE_250 and the outgoing trace. Please allocate the EUR 250 as a reconciliation adjustment on your ledger and we can either issue a supplier-side credit memo or pay an additional micro-transfer to clear the shortfall — whichever is faster for your collections process.

Attachment: [Attachment: Lumenix_Bank_Advice_071326.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

Let me know preferred approach.

Best,
Sophie

Looping in internal collections note. Diego — we can accept the reconciliation adjustment and post an internal hold tag so the customer portal shows a "payment received: pending allocation (EUR 250)" status. Laura, treasury policy is to hold for up to 10 business days for correspondent-bank shortfalls if the payer confirms fee responsibility. If Lumenix will issue a credit memo (or do a micro-remit), we'll apply and clear immediately.

Action items: 
- Sophie: confirm whether Lumenix prefers issuing a credit memo or doing the micro-remit (we'll provide a one-line SR for the micro-remit).
- Diego: please add ledger note with TRACE:7X9L-LLN and annotate the 250 as "CORRESP_FEE_RECOVERY_PENDING"
- Laura: confirm acceptance window (we have 10 business days per policy)

Vanessa Ortiz
